text: Canon Inc. (Japanese: キヤノン株式会社; Hepburn: Kyanon kabushiki gaisha) is a Japanese multinational corporation headquartered in Ōta, Tokyo, specializing in optical, imaging, and industrial products such as lenses, cameras, medical equipment, scanners, printers, and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The company has a primary listing on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the TOPIX Core 30 and Nikkei 225 indexes; it previously had a secondary listing on the New York Stock Exchange. Originally named Seikikōgaku kenkyūsho (Precision Optical Laboratory) in 1933, it became Precision Optical Instruments, Co., Ltd. in 1937 and was founded by Takeshi Mitarai, Goro Yoshida, Saburo Uchida, and Takeo Maeda. In 1934, it developed the Kwanon, a prototype for Japan's first 35mm camera with a focal-plane-based shutter, and in 1940, created Japan's first indirect X-ray camera. The company name was changed to Canon Camera Co., Inc. in 1947 and shortened to Canon Inc. in 1969. The name Canon derives from the Buddhist bodhisattva Kannon (Guanyin, Kwannon, or Kwanon). During its early years, Canon lacked facilities to produce optical glass and used Nikkor lenses from Nippon Kogaku K.K. (later Nikon). Between 1933 and 1936, the Kwanon, a copy of the Leica design, was developed in prototype form. In 1958, Canon introduced a field zoom lens for television broadcasting, and in 1959, launched the Reflex Zoom 8 and Canonflex. In 1961, it introduced the Rangefinder camera Canon 7 with a 50mm 1:0.95 lens in a special bayonet mount. In 1964, Canon released the Canola 130, Japan's first 10-key calculator, an improvement on the Bell Punch Sumlock Anita Mark 8. In 1965, it introduced the Canon Pellix, a single lens reflex (SLR) camera with a semi-transparent stationary mirror. In 1971, Canon launched the Canon F-1, a high-end SLR camera, and the FD lens range. In 1976, it introduced the Canon AE-1, the world's first camera with an embedded micro-computer. In 1985, Canon introduced its Inkjet printer using bubble-jet technology, one year after Hewlett-Packard. In 1987, it launched the Canon Electro-Optical System (EOS), named after the goddess of the dawn, along with the Canon EOS 650 autofocus SLR camera, and established the Canon Foundation. In 1988, it introduced the Kyosei philosophy. In 1989, the EOS 1 Flagship Professional SLR line was launched, and in the same year, the EOS RT, the world's first AF SLR with a fixed, semi-transparent pellicle mirror, was unveiled. In 1992, Canon launched the Canon EOS 5, the first camera with eye-controlled AF, and the PowerShot 600, its first digital camera. In 1995, it introduced the first commercially available SLR lens with internal image stabilization, the Canon EF 75-300mm lens f/4–5.6 IS USM. The Canon EOS-RS was the world's fastest AF SLR camera with a continuous shooting speed of 10 frames per second at the time, based on the EOS-1N, which had a fixed, semi-transparent pellicle mirror with a hard coat. In 1996, Canon introduced a pocket-sized digital camera using the Advanced Photo System, named ELPH in America and IXUS in Europe. In 1997, Canon entered the digital video camcorder market. In 2004, it introduced the XEED SX50 LCD projector. In 2005, it launched its first high-definition camcorder. In November 2009, Canon made a €730 million (US$1.1 billion) all-cash offer for Dutch printer maker Océ, acquired majority ownership by March 2010, and completed the 100% acquisition by the end of 2011. In 2010, Canon acquired Tereck Office Solutions, Inc. On 16 March 2010, Canon announced its intent to acquire a .canon generic top-level domain, which it acquired in February 2015 and first used on its global website in May 2016. In the third quarter of 2012, Canon's global market share for printers, copiers, and multifunction devices was 20.90%. In early 2013, Canon USA moved into a new US$500 million headquarters in Melville, New York. In February 2014, Canon announced it would acquire Texas-based Molecular Imprints Inc., a developer of nanoprint lithography systems, for an amount speculated to be around US$98 million. On 13 June 2014, Canon announced the acquisition of Danish IP Surveillance VMS software company Milestone Systems, which operates as a separate entity. On 10 February 2015, Canon announced intentions to buy Swedish Security Camera maker Axis Communications for US$2.83 billion. On 23 February 2015, Axis confirmed it had received a purchase proposal from Canon, and the purchase was effectively completed in April 2015. On 24 April 2015, Canon Europe acquired the London-based family photo sharing startup Lifecake. In November 2015, Canon USA filed litigation against camera gear retailers including Get It Digital, All New Shop, and F&E Trading to prevent the sale of gray-market camera gear. In March 2016, Canon acquired Toshiba Medical Systems Corporation for US$5.9 billion. On 28 March 2017, Canon Europe acquired the London-based printing startup Kite. On 2 April 2019, Canon introduced two new UHDgc 2/3-inch Portable Zoom Lenses designed for 4K UHD Broadcast Cameras. In July 2020, Canon recorded its first ever quarterly loss due to the COVID-19 pandemic. In September 2020, Fujitsu announced it would provide Canon with a Fujitsu Supercomputer PRIMEHPC FX1000 unit to assist with its no-prototype development manufacturing initiative. In December 2020, Canon concluded its photographic-equipment print-ad series named "Wildlife as Canon Sees It," which began in 1981 in National Geographic magazine. In October 2023, Canon introduced new nanoimprint lithography manufacturing systems, claiming they are simpler and more affordable than ASML's extreme ultraviolet lithography systems and capable of producing circuits equivalent to 5 nm scale. Canon's products include cameras (compact digital, video, film SLR, digital SLR), camcorders, lenses, broadcasting equipment (including free viewpoint solutions), professional displays, projectors, manufacturing equipment (including photolithography equipment such as steppers, scanners), printers, photocopiers, image scanners, digital microfilm scanners, fax machines, binoculars, microscopes, medical equipment (including diagnostic systems such as ultrasound, X-ray, CT and MRI scanners and ophthalmic equipment), CCTV solutions, image sensors, calculators, high-precision positioning and measurement devices (such as rotary encoders), custom optical components, handy terminals, mixed reality systems, software, and space satellites. Canon has been manufacturing and distributing digital cameras since 1984, starting with the RC-701, followed by the RC, PowerShot, and Digital IXUS series. The EOS series of digital single-lens reflex cameras (DSLRs) includes high-end professional models. Due to consumers switching from compact cameras to smartphones, Canon's Q1 2013 operating profit fell 34 percent year-on-year. Canon produces high-output flash units for DSLR cameras, including the 270EX II, 320EX, 430EX II, 430EX III-RT, 470EX-AI, 580EX, 580EX II, 600EX-RT, 600EXII-RT, EL-1, and EL-5 Speedlites, and macro flash units such as the Macro Twin Lite and Macro Ring Lite. Canon designs and manufactures CMOS image sensors in-house with three dedicated fabs in Japan. In 2016, Canon, the fifth-largest image sensor manufacturer globally, began selling sensors to other companies, though it does not plan to sell smartphone image sensors, focusing instead on industrial and space observation markets. Although Canon withdrew from the pixel count race in the 2000s, it has been at the forefront of image sensor resolution in recent years, with a 250MP sensor demo revealed in 2015 and reported for launch in 2020, and a 120MP sensor launched in 2018 as part of its B2B offerings. Canon was the principal maker of print engines in industry-standard laser printers; early Apple LaserWriter and HP LaserJet models used the Canon LBP-CX, LBP-SX, LBP-LX, LBP-EX, and LBP-PX engines. Following the 2010 acquisition of Dutch digital printing manufacturer Océ, Canon continued developing and manufacturing printing systems under the Océ brand, which was officially renamed Canon Production Printing on 1 January 2020. Canon has been sued for intentionally designing all-in-one printers that cannot scan when low on ink and settled the lawsuit in 2023 without admitting guilt. Canon's largest revenue-generating division is its multifunction copier division. It distributes consumer and home office imageCLASS products through retail outlets and professional-grade imageRUNNER series through Canon Solutions America and independent distributors. The professional-grade series ranges from small table-top units to large digital presses. Canon manufactures a wide range of flatbed, film, and document scanners for home and business use, including the Canon CanoScan 8800F, some of which use LED inDirect Exposure (LiDE) technology allowing USB power without additional power. Current printers use the proprietary BJNP protocol (USB over IP port 8611). Canon produced a range of calculators, including handheld, desktop, printing, and scientific models; the 1964 Canola 130 had 13 digits, a result of marketing research to meet Japanese central bank requirements due to the low value of the Japanese Yen. The calculator used germanium transistors and a light pipe display. Canon produces a range of projectors and offers wireless presenters, from advanced green laser presenters with back-lit screens to basic red laser clickers. Canon is developing a prototype virtual reality headset (Canon VR) with a 120° viewing angle, requiring handles instead of a head strap and not yet available for sale. As of 2020, Canon produces and sells high-end AR headsets for enterprise users. Canon is one of the world's top producers of semiconductor and display manufacturing equipment; its subsidiary Canon Tokki dominates the material deposition equipment and OLED display manufacturing instrument markets, and it is the leading manufacturer of display photolithography equipment and one of the top three in the semiconductor lithography machine market. Once a leader in semiconductor lithography alongside Nikon, Canon has been surpassed by ASML, with its market share in the overall market falling below 5% as of 2017. In 1983, Canon introduced two MSX home computer models, the V-10 and V-20, both offering minimal MSX standards; the V-20 could receive shooting data from the T90 Canon camera via the Data Memory Back T90 expansion. Canon also sold the Canon AS100 PC shortly after the IBM PC launch, based on the Intel 8088 processor and using CP/M or MS-DOS, with an option for an 8 MB hard drive. As of 2020, Canon is organized into four principal business segments. As of 31 June 2017, Canon has 383 subsidiaries, including second-generation subsidiaries such as Canon IT Solutions Inc. Its world headquarters is located at 30-2 Shimomaruko 3-chome, Ota-ku, Tokyo 146–8501, Japan, with regional headquarters in America, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Japan, Asia, and Oceania (including Australia & New Zealand). Canon Europe has two principal subsidiaries: Canon Europa NV (Amstelveen, Netherlands) and Canon Europe Ltd. (Uxbridge, UK). On 26 December 2003, Canon announced restructuring plans for three domestic Canon Group companies, involving the merger of two and the spinning off of one. In 2011, Canon generated total revenues of US$45,608 million, with 53.9% from the Office Business Unit, 36.9% from the Consumer Business Unit, and 11.8% from the Industry and Others Business Unit. Revenue distribution was 31.3% in Europe, 27.0% in the Americas, 22.2% in Asia and Oceania (excluding Japan), and 19.5% in Japan. Canon invested US$3,946 million in research and development in 2011, equivalent to 8.7% of sales, and was granted 2,813 U.S. patents that year, the third-highest number after IBM and Samsung Electronics. A report by Clean Air-Cool Planet ranked Canon at the top of a list of 56 climate-friendly companies. Canon launched three new calculators in Europe called "Green Calculators," produced in part from recycled copiers. The Canon Group has an environmental charter focused on reducing environmental burden through resource efficiency and eliminating anti-social activities threatening health and safety. In 2020, Canon joined WIPO GREEN as an official partner to address climate change. While Canon's head office is committed to preventing global warming, its subsidiary The Canon Institute for Global Studies (CIGS) appointed anthropogenic global warming skeptic Taishi Sugiyama as research director and disseminated anti-renewable energy theories. When contacted by The Guardian, Canon stated that CIGS is not a business of the company and cannot comment on its activities or research. CIGS was established in 2017 to commemorate the 70th anniversary of Canon Inc. and is chaired by the company's CEO, drawing protests from Action Speaks Louder and photographers in a “Cameras Don't Lie” contest. In 2008, Canon donated RMB 1 million to the Red Cross Society of China and RMB 10 million from Canon Inc., Japan, following the Sichuan earthquake in May 2008. In 1983, Canon became the first title sponsor of the English football league, which was named The Canon League from 1983 to 198.

Canon has been associated with anthropogenic global warming skepticism and anti-renewable energy theories through its research director, iyama, and has disseminated such views. When contacted by The Guardian, Canon stated that the Canon Institute for Global Studies (CIGS) is not a business division of the company and that it is not in a position to comment on the institute’s activities or research. CIGS was established in 2017 to mark the 70th anniversary of Canon Inc. and its chairman is Canon’s CEO, a fact that has drawn criticism from the corporate watchdog group Action Speaks Louder and photographers participating in a “Cameras Don't Lie” contest. In 2008, Canon donated financial support to assist the estimated 5 million people displaced by the earthquake in China’s Sichuan province in May 2008, contributing RMB 1 million to the Red Cross Society of China shortly after the disaster, followed by a donation of RMB 10 million from Canon Inc., Japan. In 1983, Canon became the first title sponsor of the English football league, known as The Canon League from 1983 to 1986 when the sponsorship was taken over by the Today newspaper, and also sponsored Italian football club Hellas Verona FC from 1982 to 1986, including during the 1984–85 Serie A season when they won the league. From 1967 to 2003, Canon sponsored the Greater Hartford Open, now known as the Travelers Championship. In Formula One, Canon sponsored Williams from 1985 to 1993, during which the team won World Drivers’ Championships for Nelson Piquet (1987), Nigel Mansell (1992), and Alain Prost (1993), as well as four World Constructors’ Championships (1986, 1987, 1992, 1993). Canon also sponsored Brawn GP in the 2009 Singapore Grand Prix. Between 1994 and 1997, Canon sponsored the South Sydney Rabbitohs. Since 2006, Canon has supported the Red Cross in providing assistance to 13 Red Cross National Societies across Europe, focusing on youth projects, through financial contributions, donations of imaging equipment such as cameras, copying machines, and digital radiography devices, and volunteer activities. Canon Europe has been a partner of World Press Photo for 16 years, a organization that promotes professional standards in photography, organizes the largest international contest for professional photojournalists, and serves as a global platform for press photography. Canon Asia sponsored various competitions, including the Canon Photomarathon and the reality TV show Photo Face-Off, in which professional photographer Justin Mott serves as the judge and competes against amateur photographers; Mott began filming season 3 in April 2016, and that season aired at the end of the same year. Technical specifications include pellicle mirror, APS-format, eye-controlled focus, processors such as Non-DIGIC, DIGIC, DIGIC II, DIGIC III, DIGIC 4/4+, DIGIC 5/5+, DIGIC 6/6+, DIGIC 7, DIGIC 8, and DIGIC X, video capabilities of 720p, 1080p, uncompressed 1080p, 4K, and 5.5K, screen types including flip (tilt) F, articulating A, and touchscreen T, body features including weather sealing, specialty models such as astrophotography a, Cinema EOS C, high-resolution camera S, and no AA filter effect R, and firmware add-ons including x Magic Lantern Support.
